status: drafted via multi-agent workflow, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: 1 Peter is an epistle, not narrative, so its scribe-tier structure differs from the Gospels/OT precedent: only two figures carry enough personally-embodied weight for a full person-tier (Peter, the letter's author/elder, exhorting from his own first-person experience; and Jesus Christ, whose own suffering, death, resurrection, and exaltation are described as real completed actions throughout the letter — 2:21-25 and 3:18-22 especially — even though he is not physically present acting within THIS text's own frame the way Gospel-Jesus is). Every other major content block is a law/theme tier (deliveredBy peter_1peter) named after the section's own KJV imagery (living stones, the fiery trial, etc.), since the epistle is almost entirely doctrinal exhortation rather than character-driven scenes. Minor named figures who are cited but do not act within this book (Abraham, Sarah, Noah, "the prophets" as an undifferentiated collective per rule 5) are logged as role:"named" rather than forced into submanager or law-tier slots, and are cross-referenced to their existing Genesis entries via fresh book-scoped ids per the standing id-disambiguation rule. Two tradition-vs-text flags: Marcus (5:13) is traditionally identified with John Mark/the Gospel of Mark's author, and "Babylon" (5:13) is widely read by many scholars as a cipher for Rome — 1 Peter's own text asserts neither identification, so both are noted as tradition, not fact, per the later/traditional-name rule. Peter uses a fresh book-scoped id (peter_1peter) rather than reusing any id from the OT indexing pass, per this session's instruction, since he is a New Testament epistle author with no prior indexed entry to collide with. Correction applied: the prophets_1peter verse note for 1 Peter 1:10-12 was fixed to correctly attribute the reporting of the gospel to the human preachers (empowered by/accompanied by the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven), not to the Holy Ghost as the reporting agent itself, matching the actual KJV wording of 1 Peter 1:12.

characters.name: Peter

verses.note: Introduces himself as an apostle of Jesus Christ, writing to strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
Identifies himself as also an elder, a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed.
Exhorts fellow elders to feed the flock of God willingly, not as lords over God's heritage but as examples, promising a crown of glory at the chief Shepherd's appearing.
States he has written this brief letter by Silvanus, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God.
Sends greeting from the church at Babylon and from Marcus his son, closing with a call to greet one another with a kiss of charity.

funFacts: This epistle names its recipients across five Roman provinces of Asia Minor (Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, Bithynia) rather than a single church.
This is a fresh book-scoped id distinct from any Gospel indexing of Peter (e.g. Matthew's own Peter entry) — same historical person, tracked separately per this book's own text.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.scribeTier: Christ, the Suffering and Risen Shepherd
characters.perkNote: 1 Peter's own text does not address Christ's earthly parentage or lineage at all — only his redemptive suffering, death, resurrection, and exaltation are described, so genealogy fields are left null rather than imported from Gospel material this book doesn't itself state.

verses.note: The Spirit of Christ in the prophets testified beforehand of his sufferings and the glory that should follow.
Believers are redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.
Foreordained before the foundation of the world, manifested in these last times, raised from the dead and given glory by God.
Described as a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious.
Identified with the prophesied chief corner stone in Zion — precious to believers, but a stone of stumbling to the disobedient.
Suffered for believers, leaving an example to follow; did no sin, no guile in his mouth; bore their sins in his own body on the tree, by whose stripes they were healed.
Called the Shepherd and Bishop of souls, to whom the once-straying are now returned.
Suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, put to death in the flesh but quickened by the Spirit.
By the Spirit went and preached unto the spirits in prison, who were disobedient in the days of Noah while the ark was preparing.
His resurrection is the reality baptism figures; he is gone into heaven and on the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers made subject unto him.

characters.name: Silvanus
characters.perkNote: Likely the same Silvanus/Silas who traveled with Paul (Acts 15:40, 2 Corinthians 1:19) — a plausible cross-reference, but 1 Peter's own text does not itself state this identification, so it is noted as likely, not asserted as certain.

verses.note: Called 'a faithful brother,' the one by whom Peter states he has written this brief letter, exhorting and testifying to the true grace of God.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.perkNote: Traditionally identified with John Mark, companion of Paul and Barnabas and traditional author of the Gospel of Mark — this identification is common tradition, not something 1 Peter's own text states or confirms.

verses.note: Called 'Marcus my son' by Peter, sending greeting alongside 'the church that is at Babylon.'

characters.name: Abraham
characters.perkNote: Same figure indexed at length in Genesis (id 'abraham' in that book's data file) — reused here only as an example cited in Peter's household instruction, not re-indexed with his full Genesis genealogy/verse set.

verses.note: Cited as the one Sara obeyed, 'calling him lord,' held up as an example within the instruction to wives.

characters.name: Sarah
characters.perkNote: Same figure indexed in Genesis (id 'sarah' in that book's data file) — reused here only as the cited example of a wife's godly submission, not re-indexed with her full Genesis details.

verses.note: Named among 'the holy women' of old who trusted in God, specifically noted for obeying Abraham and calling him lord.

characters.name: Noah
characters.perkNote: Same figure indexed in Genesis (id 'noah' in that book's data file) — cited here only within Peter's baptism/ark typology, not re-indexed with his full Genesis narrative.

verses.note: Referenced via 'the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water' — cited as the type Peter uses to explain baptism.

characters.name: The Prophets
characters.perkNote: Treated as one undifferentiated collective per rule 5 — the text does not name or individuate which prophets are meant.

verses.note: Described as having enquired and searched diligently, testifying beforehand of the sufferings of Christ and the glory that should follow, ministering things reported to believers by those who preached the gospel unto them, with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven.

characters.name: Living Hope and the Trial of Faith
characters.scribeTier: Living Hope and the Trial of Faith
characters.purpose: Assures suffering, scattered believers of an incorruptible heavenly inheritance reserved for them, and explains that present trials test and refine genuine faith the way fire refines gold — a salvation so significant that even the prophets searched to understand it and angels desired to look into it.

verses.note: Believers are begotten again unto a lively hope by Christ's resurrection, unto an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, reserved in heaven.
Manifold temptations/trials are described as testing faith, more precious than gold that perishes, though it be tried with fire.
Believers who love Christ unseen rejoice, receiving the end of their faith, the salvation of their souls.
The prophets searched diligently concerning this salvation, and angels desire to look into these things.

characters.name: Be Ye Holy: The New Birth
characters.scribeTier: Be Ye Holy: The New Birth
characters.purpose: Calls believers to personal holiness matching God's own holiness, grounded in the fact that they were redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, and that they have been born again by the incorruptible word of God rather than by perishable means.

verses.note: Exhortation to gird up the loins of the mind, be sober, and be holy in all manner of conversation, as God who called them is holy.
Instructs passing the time of sojourning in fear, since they were redeemed not with corruptible silver or gold but the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish.
Purified souls should love one another fervently, being born again not of corruptible seed but by the word of God which liveth and abideth for ever — 'all flesh is as grass.'

characters.name: Living Stones, A Royal Priesthood
characters.purpose: Defines the corporate identity of believers as a spiritual house and royal priesthood built upon Christ the living/chief corner stone, called out of darkness into God's marvellous light to show forth his praises.

verses.note: Instructs laying aside malice and desiring the sincere milk of the word, having tasted that the Lord is gracious.
Believers, coming to Christ the living stone, are themselves built up as lively stones into a spiritual house, an holy priesthood.
Describes believers as a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people, once not a people but now the people of God.

characters.name: Submission to Every Ordinance of Man
characters.scribeTier: Submission to Every Ordinance of Man
characters.purpose: Instructs believers to submit to civil authority and honor the king for the Lord's sake, so that good conduct silences the ignorance of foolish men, while treating their Christian liberty as service to God rather than a cover for wrongdoing.

verses.note: Urges abstaining from fleshly lusts and maintaining honest conduct among the Gentiles.
Submit to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as supreme or to governors, so as to silence foolish men by well-doing.
As free, but not using liberty as a cloak of maliciousness; honour all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the king.

characters.name: Household Order: Servants, Wives, and Husbands
characters.scribeTier: Household Order: Servants, Wives, and Husbands
characters.purpose: Gives household-specific instruction: servants are to submit to masters even when treated unjustly, and wives and husbands are to honor one another within marriage, with Sarah's obedience to Abraham cited as an example of godly submission and husbands told to honor wives as fellow heirs of the grace of life.

verses.note: Servants are told to be subject to masters with all fear, even the froward, since it is thankworthy to suffer wrongfully for conscience toward God.
Wives are to be in subjection to their own husbands, so that even disobedient husbands may be won without a word by their conduct.
Adorning should not be merely outward, but the hidden man of the heart, a meek and quiet spirit.
Cites the holy women of old, including Sara obeying Abraham, calling him lord.
Husbands are told to dwell with their wives according to knowledge, giving honour as unto the weaker vessel and as heirs together of the grace of life, so their prayers not be hindered.

characters.name: Suffering for Well-Doing
characters.purpose: Calls believers to unity, compassion, and blessing rather than reviling when wronged, to sanctify Christ as Lord in their hearts and be ready to give a meek answer for their hope, since it is better to suffer for well-doing than for evil-doing.

verses.note: Be of one mind, having compassion, love as brethren, not rendering evil for evil or railing for railing, but blessing instead.
He that would love life must refrain his tongue from evil, since the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous.
Those who follow good need not fear harm, and are blessed even if they suffer for righteousness' sake.
Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asks a reason of your hope, with meekness and fear.
It is better, if God so wills, to suffer for well-doing than for evil-doing.

characters.name: Stewards of the Manifold Grace of God
characters.scribeTier: Stewards of the Manifold Grace of God
characters.purpose: Exhorts believers to arm themselves with the same mind as Christ's suffering to cease from sin, live the rest of their time for God's will rather than fleshly lusts, and use whatever gift each has received to minister to one another as faithful stewards of God's manifold grace.

verses.note: Arm yourselves likewise with the same mind, since he that has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, and should no longer live to the lusts of men.
The end of all things is at hand, calling for watchfulness in prayer and fervent charity, since charity covers the multitude of sins.
Use hospitality without grudging; minister whatever gift received as good stewards of the manifold grace of God, speaking as the oracles of God.

characters.name: The Fiery Trial
characters.purpose: Reassures believers not to think it strange when suffering intensifies into a 'fiery trial,' but to rejoice as partakers of Christ's sufferings, and explains that judgment beginning at the house of God means the righteous are tested first — so sufferers should commit their souls to God in well-doing.

verses.note: Believers should not think it strange concerning the fiery trial, but rejoice as partakers of Christ's sufferings.
Being reproached for the name of Christ is called a happy state, since the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon them.
Warns against suffering as an evildoer, but not being ashamed to suffer as a Christian, glorifying God in that name.
Judgment must begin at the house of God; sufferers according to God's will should commit the keeping of their souls to him in well-doing, as unto a faithful Creator.

characters.name: Humility and Resisting the Adversary
characters.purpose: Instructs younger believers to submit to elders and all to be clothed with humility, since God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble; calls believers to cast their care upon God and stay sober and vigilant, since their adversary the devil seeks to devour them, and to resist him steadfast in faith.

verses.note: Younger believers are told to submit to the elder, and all to be subject one to another, clothed with humility, since God resists the proud.
Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, casting all your care upon him, for he cares for you.
Be sober and vigilant, since the adversary the devil walks about as a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour; resist him steadfast in the faith.
The God of all grace, who called believers to eternal glory by Christ Jesus, will after suffering a while make them perfect, stablish, strengthen, and settle them.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

babylonChurch.note: 'The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you' — many scholars read this as a symbolic cipher for Rome, but 1 Peter's own text does not state this identification, so it is left as an unresolved location/community reference rather than asserted as Rome.

angels.note: Angels are noted as desiring to look into the things of this salvation — a brief mention, not indexed as a tracked character.
